plan.summary: This 4-week block is the first building phase of a 12-week off-camp boxing plan with one S&C session per week. Week 1 establishes a training baseline with a simple squat assessment so later loading can be adjusted well. Weeks 2-4 build general lower-body and full-body strength and power with low-complexity exercises that fit a beginner and minimal home setup.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Establish a baseline and build general strength and power with simple movements that do not interfere too much with boxing work.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main strength work gradually while keeping one crisp power element and recoverable accessory volume.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift more of the session toward fast explosive output while keeping enough strength work to hold onto the gains.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a quiet landing. Reset between reps and stop if height drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is tight. Start from a still quarter squat and jump fast.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low safe box only if landing quality is good.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up progressively, then work up to your hardest clean set of 3-5 reps with good depth and control. This sets your starting strength baseline for the next weeks.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can set your starting baseline.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if your heaviest kettlebell or dumbbell is too light.

substitutionOptions.name: Sandbag Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: A good option if a sandbag is your main load at home.

exercises.name: 1a. Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Keep a soft knee bend, push the hips back, and feel the hamstrings load. Stop before your back rounds.

substitutionOptions.name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use one or two kettlebells with the same hinge pattern.

substitutionOptions.name: Band Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if load options are limited and keep the tempo controlled.

exercises.name: 1b. One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Brace hard and pull the elbow toward the hip. Do not twist through the torso.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Safer and easier to control if you have a bench.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a loaded backpack if dumbbells are limited.

exercises.name: 2a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Keep the body straight and lower under control. Elevate the hands if needed so every rep stays clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Best option if full floor push-ups are too hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if wrists do not like push-ups.

exercises.name: 2b. Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace the ribs down, squeeze the glutes, and keep the body in one straight line.

substitutionOptions.name: Body Saw Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Slightly harder option if the basic plank is easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if planks irritate the lower back.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.notes: Walk tall with a tight midline and even steps. Use a load you can hold without leaning.

substitutionOptions.name: Suitcase Carry
substitutionOptions.notes: Great option with one dumbbell or kettlebell. Switch sides each set.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Rack Carry
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if grip is the limiting factor.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump fast and land softly. Rest enough to keep every rep sharp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Good option if ceiling height is limited.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a safe low box and step down each rep.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Use the heaviest load you can control for all sets with clean depth. Leave 2 reps in reserve on the first 3 sets and 1-2 reps in reserve on the last set.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set of 6 with full depth and stable posture.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you outgrow the goblet hold.

substitutionOptions.name: Sandbag Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Works well when home loading options are limited.

exercises.name: 1a. Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Drive the hips back and keep the dumbbells close to the legs. Move with control and stand tall at the top.

substitutionOptions.name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use one or two kettlebells in the same rep range.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if your balance is solid and loading is limited.

exercises.name: 1b. One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Keep the shoulder packed and pull smoothly. Pause briefly at the top.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: More stable and easier to coach well.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Useful if adjustable dumbbells are not available.

exercises.name: 2a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a version that lets you keep 1-2 reps in reserve with clean body position.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this to keep form strong through all reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: A solid substitute if pushing on the floor is awkward.

exercises.name: 2b. Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Press the lower back into the floor and breathe shallow behind the brace.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Simpler option if the hollow hold is too demanding.

substitutionOptions.name: Bent-Knee Hollow Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot keep the lower back down.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.notes: Walk under control and keep the torso stacked. If grip fades badly, shorten the distance slightly.

substitutionOptions.name: Suitcase Carry
substitutionOptions.notes: Good with one implement. Alternate sides evenly.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Rack Carry
substitutionOptions.notes: Useful if you want more trunk demand with less grip fatigue.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Every rep should be explosive. Stop the set if jump height clearly drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a simpler jump pattern.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a safe low box and prioritize a quiet landing.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Add a small amount of load from last week if all sets were solid. Keep 1-2 reps in reserve and make every rep look the same.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the heaviest clean set of 5 you can complete with full depth and no form breakdown.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the goblet position limits loading.

substitutionOptions.name: Sandbag Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: A practical home option if sandbag loading is available.

exercises.name: 1a. Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Keep tension in the hamstrings and stay long through the spine. Do not turn it into a squat.

substitutionOptions.name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use one or two kettlebells with the same setup.

substitutionOptions.name: Band Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if external load is limited.

exercises.name: 1b. One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Pull hard without jerking. Keep the neck relaxed and the torso steady.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Best choice if you want less lower-back involvement.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Good home replacement when dumbbells are limited.

exercises.name: 2a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a progression that lets you own the top and bottom positions. Stop before hips sag or the head reaches first.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Keep this option if floor reps are still inconsistent.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Reliable substitute when wrist comfort is an issue.

exercises.name: 2b. Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep the ribcage down and legs only as low as you can control.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow position is too hard to maintain.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need an easier trunk option.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.notes: Move with short controlled steps and a tall posture. This should challenge your grip without pulling you out of position.

substitutionOptions.name: Suitcase Carry
substitutionOptions.notes: Great one-arm option for extra anti-rotation work.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Rack Carry
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if available loading is easier to rack than hold at the sides.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Keep the reps quick and fresh. This is a low-fatigue speed reminder, not a grind.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Simple replacement if needed.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if the setup is safe and easy.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Use the same load as Week 3 or slightly lighter and leave 2-3 reps in reserve. Move well and stay crisp.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the smoothest strong set of 5 this week and use it as your checkpoint before the next block.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a more comfortable loading position.

substitutionOptions.name: Sandbag Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Good home substitute with the same squat emphasis.

exercises.name: 1a. Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Keep the hinge pattern clean and stop the set well before fatigue changes your position.

substitutionOptions.name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use one or two kettlebells if that setup is easier.

substitutionOptions.name: Band Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Light option if you need a lower-stress week.

exercises.name: 1b. One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Smooth reps with a small pause at the top. Do not chase fatigue this week.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Stable and easy to recover from.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Useful if equipment is limited.

exercises.name: 2a. Push-Up

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Low-stress substitute if needed.

exercises.name: 2b. Front Plank
exercises.notes: Stay long and braced. This is just enough trunk work to maintain position and control.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if planks feel stale or uncomfortable.

substitutionOptions.name: Hollow Body Hold

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.notes: Carry with posture and control. Keep the load moderate and finish fresh.

substitutionOptions.name: Suitcase Carry

substitutionOptions.name: Front Rack Carry
substitutionOptions.notes: Fine option if side carries are awkward with your equipment.
